title: Contributing to officequarto
text: officequarto real R package — pure-logic unit tests run testthat/ R CMD check like package: Two checks stay outside automatic suite, since need live quarto render real .docx external quarto CLI (appropriate R CMD check, must run clean, offline environment): officequarto.crossref.auto-number also dedicated end--end fixture, kept separate template/ since template/_quarto.yml sets crossref.numbered: false (mutually exclusive auto-number design): Editing file R/ requires reinstalling package (devtools::install(), see ) next quarto render picks change — unlike template/report.qmd, plain Quarto document rendered fresh every time. dev/make-sample-docx.R regenerates sample template template/original.docx, including ACME custom styles used style-mapping (requires R packages officer xml2, generating sample template, hook ). Building pkgdown site locally (e.g. preview vignette changes):
code: devtools::document()   # (re-)generate NAMESPACE/man after any roxygen change devtools::test()       # runs every tests/testthat/test-*.R devtools::check()      # full R CMD check Rscript -e 'devtools::document(quiet = TRUE); devtools::install(quiet = TRUE, upgrade = FALSE)' cd template quarto render report.qmd Rscript ../dev/check-writeback.R   # checks header/footer/body/metadata/style-mapping/pruning of the result cd dev/fixtures/auto-number quarto render report.qmd Rscript ../../check-auto-number-e2e.R pkgdown::build_site()

title: Package architecture
text: Pandoc/Quarto render .qmd original.docx reference-doc. alone enough carry original’s styles, header, footer, section properties — ’s native Pandoc behavior, custom code involved. post-render hook runs automatically (thin shim _extensions/officequarto/scripts/writeback.R calls package’s exported oq_writeback()): resolves path reference-doc via quarto inspect, works copy freshly rendered .docx temporary directory, transfers docProps/core.xml (subject, keywords, description, category) docProps/custom.xml (freely defined custom properties) original — metadata Pandoc otherwise replaces fresh, empty values rendering. result overwrites .docx produced Quarto place; original (reference-doc) left untouched. officequarto.keep-rendered: true, plain, unpatched Pandoc output additionally saved beforehand <name>.quarto-rendered.docx (analogous Quarto’s keep-md — handy debugging, see Pandoc produced without hook). also strips style definitions word/styles.xml Pandoc added aren’t present reference-doc (see vignette("options")’s “Style pruning” section).

title: Package architecture
text: original plan (strip original’s body, insert rendered content). spike showed reference-doc already handles completely body — additional XML merge step officer added value also ran edge-case bug officer 0.7.3 merging two structurally similar documents. Details dev/spike-notes.md.

title: Configuring officequarto
text: Pandoc renders body paragraphs using styles defined reference-doc, , fixed style names (depending context, e.g. Normal, FirstParagraph, Compact) rather , possibly differently named style template (e.g. Fließtext German corporate template). officequarto.styles.body lets customize — analogous {officedown}’s mapstyles/Normal mapping: provide style name visible Word UI (internal style ID) — hook resolves word/styles.xml reference-doc. Body paragraphs detected via allowlist known Pandoc body roles (Normal, FirstParagraph, Compact, BodyText/ Body Text). configured style name doesn’t exist reference-doc, hook aborts list available paragraph styles instead silently ignoring misconfiguration. allowlist never matches footnote/endnote text, even though otherwise reachable style-mapping mechanisms — see Footnotes endnotes .
code: format:   docx:     reference-doc: original.docx     officequarto:       styles:         body: "Fließtext ACME"   # real style name from original.docx

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.lists mirrors officequarto.styles.body list paragraphs — analogous {officedown}’s ol.style/ul.style: three fields optional independent; roles aren’t configured stay Pandoc’s default styles. List paragraphs detected via presence <w:numPr> (style name, since Pandoc uses style regardless list type). List type distinguished via word/numbering.xml (w:numFmt): bullet → list-bullet; lowerLetter/upperLetter (markdown ./. markers) → list-letter; anything else (decimal, roman numerals, …) → list-number.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       lists:         list-bullet: "Aufzählung ACME"         list-number: "Nummerierung ACME"         list-letter: "Buchstabierung ACME"    # a/b/c or A/B/C lists - officequarto-only, no officedown equivalent

title: Configuring officequarto
text: list-bullet/list-number/list-letter also accepts array style names instead single value — one style per nesting level, index 0 = top level: nesting level deeper array clamps deepest configured entry — convention Word’s built-styles use (List Bullet/List Bullet 2/List Bullet 3: nothing beyond level 3 either, deeper indents just keep reusing ). plain scalar still works exactly (style every level) — officequarto-extension, {officedown} per-nesting-level equivalent ol.style/ul.style.
code: officequarto:   lists:     list-bullet: ["Aufzählung ACME", "Aufzählung ACME 2", "Aufzählung ACME 3"]

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto uses , descriptive option names (e.g. list-bullet/list-number) rather copying {officedown}’s option names verbatim. ’re coming {officedown}, though, original option names remain usable aliases officequarto.lists section, don’t relearn names already know: canonical name alias set different values, canonical name wins hook logs warning naming discarded alias value. See Option reference full canonical-name/alias table (filled incrementally {officedown} option groups ported).
code: officequarto:   lists:     list-bullet: "Aufzählung ACME"   # canonical name     # ul_style: "Aufzählung ACME"    # ...or the officedown alias — same effect

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables lets control every table rendered document formatted — analogous {officedown}’s tables option, ported first group broader {officedown}-option port (see Option reference): three fields independently optional (per-field opt-, like officequarto.styles/ officequarto.lists) — unset field left exactly Pandoc rendered , ’s forced fallback officedown’s defaults. style resolved reference-doc’s table styles (paragraph styles), fail-loud lookup body/list-bullet/etc. layout/width written directly onto every table’s w:tblPr (w:tblLayout/w:tblW), inserted OOXML-schema order alongside whatever w:tblPr children Pandoc already produced. officedown’s tab.lp option (bookdown cross-reference label-prefix) deliberately ported — ’s authoring-syntax concept equivalent Quarto already resolved cross-references hook ever runs. need change visible “Table”/“Figure” caption prefix text, use Quarto’s native crossref.tbl-title/crossref.fig-title _quarto.yml instead — officequarto option needed .
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       tables:         style: "Tabelle ACME"    # Word table style name, resolved like officequarto.styles.body         layout: fixed            # "autofit" or "fixed"         width: 0.8                # relative to page width (0..1)         # tables_style/tables_layout/tables_width also work as officedown aliases, same         # conflict rule as officequarto.lists' ol_style/ul_style (see officedown aliases above)

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables.conditional controls Word’s “Table Style Options” checkboxes (Header Row, Total Row, First/Last Column, Banded Rows/Columns) — variant table style’s conditional formatting gets applied table: field independently optional, style/layout/width. band-rows/band-columns officequarto’s , positively-phrased names officedown’s no_hband/no_vband — officedown aliases (tables_conditional_no_hband/tables_conditional_no_vband) still work carry opposite polarity (no_hband: false means thing band-rows: true); hook resolves negates correctly, including conflict warning set contradictory values.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       tables:         conditional:           first-row: true       # highlight header row           first-column: false           last-row: false           last-column: false           band-rows: true       # alternating row shading           band-columns: false

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables.caption controls table captions formatted — analogous {officedown}’s tables.caption: field independently optional. style remaps Pandoc’s caption paragraph role way code-block remaps SourceCode — tables specifically, TableCaption plain markdown caption (: caption, crossref ID) ImageCaption role shared figures Quarto crossref-managed one ({#tbl-xyz}); officequarto detects structure applies touches paragraphs structurally identified table captions, figure ones — see dev/spike-notes.md (Spike L) empirical trail. prefix/separator/number-bold inherently fragile everything else officequarto, ’s worth understanding : Quarto’s docx table captions currently render static, already-baked-text (e.g. "Table 1: caption" single text run), real Word field — ’s live number hook . officequarto rewrites text fact locating sequential table number printed (counting captioned tables document order, way Quarto numbers ) splicing configured prefix/separator around . one part Pandoc’s generated text approach doesn’t try predict shape auto-generated prefix — can vary crossref.tbl-title/title-delim settings, additionally reshaped Pandoc’s smart-typography conversion (e.g. configured -- becomes real “–” character, non-breaking space number) — rather reconstructing string config, officequarto anchors number (immune typographic conversion) find split point. caption doesn’t match expected “prefix + number + separator + text” shape, ’s left untouched rather guessed . Note applies Quarto crossref-numbered caption first place — plain markdown caption ({#tbl-xyz}) never auto-numbered Quarto , ’s generated prefix split ; style still applies , prefix/separator/number-bold make sense numbered captions. officedown’s tnd/tns (per-section numbering depth, e.g. "2-1") ported — Quarto numbers tables globally, per heading section, ’s existing per-section counter key ; replicating mean officequarto tracking heading boundaries maintaining numbering scheme, substantially larger feature direct precedent elsewhere project.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       tables:         caption:           style: "Beschriftung ACME"            # paragraph style for the caption           prefix: "Tab. "                       # text before the number (officedown: pre)           separator: " -- "                     # text between number and caption (officedown: sep)           number-bold: true                     # bold the "prefix + number" portion only

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.plots controls paragraph holding figure — analogous {officedown}’s plots option: fields independently optional, per-field opt-everywhere else. Figure paragraphs detected presence w:drawing (style name — Pandoc reuses context-dependent role names image paragraphs body text, e.g. Compact, verified empirically; officequarto.styles.body explicitly excludes drawing-paragraphs two features don’t compete paragraph). officedown’s fig.lp dropped reason tab.lp (see ) — Quarto/post-render equivalent. topcaption (caption position) implemented together tables figures — see Caption position .
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       plots:         style: "Abbildung ACME"   # paragraph style for the image paragraph         align: right               # "left", "center", or "right"

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.plots.caption mirrors table captions exactly — fields, text-parsing approach caveats, tnd/tns exclusion rationale, just figures. Unlike tables, Pandoc always uses ImageCaption role figure captions, without crossref ID: Table figure captions structurally distinguished direct positional adjacency (table caption immediately followed table; figure caption immediately preceded image paragraph) — see Table captions full mechanism; actual text-rewriting logic shared code, paragraph-finding differs.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       plots:         caption:           style: "Abbildungsbeschriftung ACME"           prefix: "Abb. "           separator: " | "           number-bold: false

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables.caption officequarto.plots.caption accept field (officedown: topcaption) moves caption paragraph table/figure: Worth knowing reach : Pandoc’s , unconfigured default already matches {officedown}’s per-type default (tables: caption ; figures: caption ) — needs setting want override default, e.g. force table’s caption . Leave unset otherwise. lives caption rather top-level officequarto.tables/officequarto.plots field, grouped rest caption options since ’s affects.
code: officequarto:   tables:     caption:       above: false   # move the table caption after the table (Pandoc's own default is already "above")   plots:     caption:       above: true    # move the figure caption before the image (Pandoc's own default is already "below")

"                            # text before the number           separator: " | "                           # text between number and caption           number-bold: false                         # explicit "not bold" (overrides any inherited bold)           above: true                                 # move the caption before the image (Pandoc's default is already "below")

Instead, one two things happens, verified real rendered output: reference-doc defines built-footnote-text style, Pandoc already reuses style’s (possibly localized) ID directly — mechanism documented blockquotes Free-form style mapping . officequarto configuration needed possible ; ’s already correct. reference-doc defines footnote-text style (like project’s sample original.docx), Pandoc falls back fixed, un-localized OOXML reserved style ID FootnoteText (EndnoteText endnotes) — Word built-style ID recognized natively even without explicit <w:style> definition. give footnotes styling case, redirect like Pandoc-invented style via officequarto.style-map: footnote/endnote paragraph style (w:pStyle, body-text formatting) covered. footnote/endnote marker character style (FootnoteReference/EndnoteReference, small superscript number) isn’t remapped officequarto — scope now. word/comments.xml still touched style-mapping mechanism (read, style-pruning reference counting).

title: Configuring officequarto
text: Page size margins already carry reference-doc natively via Pandoc — like everything else, configuration needed . officequarto.page exists different case: overriding without editing reference-doc . Pandoc’s docx writer YAML knob (unlike LaTeX/PDF writer’s geometry options), patches w:sectPr/w:pgSz/w:pgMar directly, analogous {officedown}’s page_size/page_margins: Values inches (matching officedown), converted internally twips OOXML. Every field independently optional, applied uniformly every section document (documents exactly one w:sectPr; document genuinely different per-section layouts isn’t target scenario , officedown’s single-section assumption). Setting orientation automatically swap width/height — ’re responsible consistent dimensions, officedown. officequarto.page single combined section (unlike officedown’s separate page_size/ page_margins), size/margins sub-groups — consistent officequarto.tables groups conditional/caption together rather splitting top-level sections. officedown’s orient spelled orientation ; alias remains page_size_orient (officedown’s actual literal option name, needed verbatim regardless new spelling).
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       page:         size:           width: 11.7      # inches           height: 8.3           orientation: landscape   # "portrait" or "landscape"         margins:           top: 0.75         # inches           bottom: 0.75           left: 1           right: 1           header: 0.4           footer: 0.4           gutter: 0

title: officequarto 0.1.0
text: Initial development version. yet CRAN. Converted project proper R package (officequarto), Quarto extension powers bundled inside inst/_extensions/. R package now required runtime dependency: extension’s post-render hook thin shim calls package’s exported oq_writeback(). Added oq_create_project() scaffold new officequarto project R (modeled usethis::create_project()), copying bundled extension, optional reference document, _quarto.yml listing every officequarto option default value. Paragraph style-mapping body text lists (officequarto.styles, officequarto.lists), including per-nesting-level list styles officedown-compatible option aliases. Table options: style/layout/width, conditional formatting, captions (officequarto.tables). Figure options: style/alignment captions (officequarto.plots). Caption position control (caption.) tables figures. Free-form style remapping (officequarto.style-map), including footnote/endnote paragraph styling. Page size/margins (officequarto.page). Cross-reference text control (officequarto.crossref.numbered) live, renumbering Word SEQ/REF fields (officequarto.crossref.auto-number). Added automatic style pruning: styles Pandoc adds absent reference-doc removed rendered .docx, opt-escape hatch code-block styling (officequarto.pandoc-styles.code-block). Added vignette("architecture") vignette("options"), pkgdown site published main. Added support using {officer}’s run/paragraph/block constructors (ftext(), fp_par(), block_pour_docx(), …) directly inline R expressions .qmd, way {officedown} supports .Rmd — registers knit_print methods {officer}’s S3 classes works without needing {officedown} . See vignette("officer-syntax"). fp_par()’s misplaced w:pPr fragment (structural necessity inline mechanism, shared {officedown}) automatically merged back paragraph’s real w:pPr render. Fixed: rendered .docx fail open Word entirely, two independent causes, visible real Word (python-docx/XML well-formedness checks, stayed silent): scratch comparison directory (__original__/) leaking final .docx’s zip archive, paragraph ending one w:pPr (fp_par() inline syntax, independently Pandoc’s caption-wrapper-cell paragraphs) now detected merged one, unconditionally, regardless officequarto.* configuration.
